section: Red flags: 2024 ministerial complaint over the delayed refurbishment
problems: not a dispute: the August 2024 remark was made in passing at the Molepolole museum project (Ntsweng), in one sentence of a BOPA piece about that project; no overrun, audit finding or objector is reported for the Gaborone refurbishment
repetition: P33 million, the 2020 groundbreaking, the mid-2021 completion date, the contractors and the 2022 delay are already in the record's FUNDING points
heading states a 'complaint' the page does not report as one
before:
ID: botswana-national-museum-and-art-gallery

Red flags: 2024 ministerial complaint over the delayed refurbishment
- At the groundbreaking on 18 August 2020, the environment and tourism minister Philda Kereng said the government had funded the refurbishment of the museum's permanent exhibition with P33 million and that the work was expected to be completed by mid-2021 (Daily News, BOPA, 20 August 2020).
- The project was awarded to a citizen joint venture, H&L Design Architects & Motaki Joint Venture, and the acting director of the Department of National Museum and Monuments, Stephen Mogotsi, called it "long overdue" (Daily News, BOPA, 20 August 2020).
- In August 2024 the tourism minister Dumezweni Mthimkhulu said the refurbishment of the National Museum in Gaborone was behind schedule and called this heartbreaking; he said he was disappointed that government projects were not completed on time and within budget (Daily News, BOPA, 15 August 2024).

CRITICISM IN ART MEDIA
1. Mmegi: Sandy Grant, "The National Museum: Tragedy and humiliation" (2018)
URL: https://www.mmegi.bw/ampArticle/203342
- Grant writes that in its 50th anniversary year the museum had been effectively closed for at least four years, and asks how the country could have "allowed its flag ship National Museum to become so embarrassingly dysfunctional".
- He traces the decline to the 1967 Act: for most of its 50 years the museum had no Board, and the Act does not state the museum's objectives.
- He writes that with the minister, the permanent secretary and the director all "disinterested", the museum "could only slide downward".

- https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/57883 (state outlet)
- https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/81158 (state outlet)
- https://www.mmegi.bw/ampArticle/203342
